courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio I
courses.description: This first studio course trains students in Landscape Architecture design principles towards sustainable design, situating them in the language of the discipline by introducing them to contemporary landscape theories and discourses. Appropriately scaled design projects explore issues of context, programme, landscape forms and processes as well as landscape design representation. Studio-based teaching comprises regular coursework presentation in critical review sessions. Field trips allow students to gain first-hand experience in encountering landscape designs in-situ. This master-level course consolidates proficiency in landscape design skills, enabling students to master an iterative, reflective design process, and produce design propositions with reason, imagination and ecological sensitivity within limited time.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Develop complex landscape architectural propositions that strategically apply Nature-Based Solutions, with a rigorous understanding of the site's complex ecological, social, and policy contexts.
2. Develop the ability to frame and pursue a design research inquiry that leads to an innovative strategic framework for intervention.
3. Develop the communication skills related to the conceptual, spatial, and systemic aspects of landscape strategy through diagrams, strategic maps, reports, and verbal presentations.
4. Develop a capacity for critical inquiry and collaborative exploration, using the design process to mediate and synthesize diverse disciplinary perspectives and stakeholder interests.
5. Develop a rigorous design methodology that is grounded in the School’s commitment to placing Nature and People at the center of design, enabling the formulation of a critical and socially responsible design position.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio II
courses.description: The second studio course expands the scale, scope and complexity of landscape design issues investigated. Design projects will encompass larger sites to address more complex urban-rural sustainable design issues. Students will improve their design skills to articulate more considered proposals in terms of design language, responses to site and project brief, socio-economic considerations and disciplinary understanding. There may be interaction with related planning issues and engineering technologies, as well as possible collaborative learning with related disciplines such as architecture and urban design. Students will learn to develop innovative proposals using sustainable and ecological design principles.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Articulate and justify design decisions based on their social and ecological impacts, demonstrating a critical understanding of the landscape architect’s agency in prioritizing Nature and People.
2. Develop the ability to advance a design project from strategic concept to detailed resolution through rigorous research, testing, and iterative refinement.
3. Develop the communication skills related to the technical, spatial, and performative aspects of the design through detailed drawings, technical specifications, physical/digital models, and verbal communication.
4. Develop the ability to critically integrate advanced technical knowledge from specialist consultants into a cohesive and resolved design proposal.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Topical Studies in Rural Revitalisation

meetings.location: Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G01
meetings.instructor: Professor CHUNG Wang Leung Thomas Tommy

meetings.location: Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G01
meetings.instructor: Professor CHUNG Wang Leung Thomas Tommy

courses.description: This course explores theories and ideas of landscape heritage, proactive conservation and holistic regeneration. Students will research and work on real‐life projects of rural revitalisation Hong Kong’s remote countryside, visiting actual sites and meeting villagers and stakeholders. Students will understand, experience and participate in the rural revitalization of Hong Kong’s eco‐cultural landscape. Students will 1) research rural conservation practices and policies local and abroad; 2) document, map and study landscape and fabric conditions; 3) develop sustainable design strategies and regenerative prototypes on site while consulting with villagers and experts from relevant disciplines.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture, MSc in Urban Design and MArch.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:

1. Research rural conservation practices and policies, both locally and abroad.
2. Document, map, and study existing landscape and cultural fabric conditions.
3. Develop sustainable design strategies and regenerative prototypes in consultation with villagers and interdisciplinary experts.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Ecology and Planting in Landscape Design

meetings.location: Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G04

courses.description: This course covers essential fundamental knowledge and skills for landscape practitioners in sustainable design regarding biophysical systems, ecology and horticulture, and their effective impacts on the design process. Ecological principles and concepts, impacts of land developments on urban ecology and ecosystem processes will be introduced. Key content will comprise vegetation types and habitats, a comprehensive understanding of plant species and plant communities in Hong Kong and Southern China, together with basic principles and vocabulary of plant identification, planting design and horticultural maintenance.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:

1. Develop a macro understanding of ecology to analyze environmental systems and their interrelationships across scales.
2. Apply this integrated understanding to design high-performance, Nature-Based Solutions and functional plant communities.
3. Leverage ecological knowledge to frame and justify design interventions in economic terms.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Urban and Landscape History and Theory
courses.description: This course explores the history of urbanization and landscape and its theories, examining why and how cities and landscapes evolved with respect to their geographical and cultural contexts, while also considering more recent and contemporary cases of urban and landscape design that respond to more pressing ecological questions and more recent ecological frameworks such as the UN SDGs. The lectures are organized into themes that is roughly chronological, while focusing on topical issues to stimulate discussions and debates within the class.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes: This course will provide students with skills to understand complex forces that shape cities, and introduces critical methods and tools to describe and theorize the urban processes that influence the built environment. Using a themed approach and in-depth case studies, students will learn to articulate the relationship between visual and physical form of the urban environment and urban settings, processes and contexts in different perspectives, styles and methods of inquiry.
